progressAppend: R54 separated stable color storage from cutoff and blending. Under pinned Three.js r186 / Chromium 143 direct software WebGL and confirmed WebGPU, 256 stable one-pixel samples (1024 channels) were rendered to offscreen RGBA32F and RGBA8 with NoToneMapping and NoColorSpace on the targets. Maximum normalized float-to-RGBA8 error was 0.0019607962346544494 on both backends, about half an 8-bit code plus float epsilon; no channel exceeded one code. WebGL/WebGPU float-target hashes matched exactly and final-target hashes matched exactly. The R54 machine gate passed. This does not cover Gaussian blend accumulation, presentation transforms, hardware GPU, Apple target devices, real assets or human acceptance.
nextGate: Build a controlled direct Three.js r186 two-splat source-over blend comparison using a blendable float intermediate and RGBA8 final target. Preserve locked draw order and blend factors, and keep stable pixels separate from cutoff-neighbor pixels. Then test browser presentation/color transforms independently. Hardware-backed WebGPU and Apple Safari/WebKit remain explicit infrastructure-dependent Unknowns; do not substitute SwiftShader repetition for hardware evidence. Only after the user supplies a small static photo set should the COLMAP/Brush/PLY/SPZ/r186 pilot run under accumulated R34-R54 gates.
